first_impression.reaction: Googled 'wedding in crete' because it's on our shortlist and I want to know what I'm walking into. The intro gets straight to month, end of the island and cost, with no 'turquoise paradise' rubbish, so I kept going. I jumped to the FAQ first like I always do, then the cost section, because that's where the catch usually is. The cost section actually names the catches: a three-night minimum stay, room blocks, package items you can't swap, fees charged on top. Then a proper weather table with the source and the years. That's more evidence than most planner blogs give me. My gripes are small: the timeline reads like Greek law but it's really one resort's rules, the 'is Crete good' FAQ answer is all upside, and I still don't know how you pick the venues you 'recommend'.

journey.quote: Crete is on your shortlist, and the questions now are practical ones: which month, which end of the island, and what moves the cost.
journey.reaction: Good. That's exactly my list, and nobody's tried to sell me a sunset yet.

Went to the FAQ first. Every other answer is straight, but this one only gives the upsides. The page itself tells me about 30-plus degree summers, wildfire season and a three-hour drive across the island. Put those in here too and I'd believe the 'yes' more.

journey.quote: Yes. Venues such as the Elounda Collection offer civil packages, and the marriage is registered at the local Registry Office after the ceremony.
journey.reaction: A direct answer, then the Australian recognition point. That's how a FAQ should read.

journey.quote: The table below sets out long-term averages from the Hellenic National Meteorological Service for two stations: Heraklion on the central north coast (1955 to 2010) and Souda, near Chania in the west (1958 to 2010).
journey.reaction: Named source, named stations, date range. That's a table I can actually check, and the numbers line up with what they say underneath.

journey.quote: These are long-term averages, not a forecast; any single week can run hotter, cooler or wetter.
journey.reaction: Honest about the limits of its own data. Rare.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises that wildfires occur in Greece during the extended summer period from June to September, including near cities and tourist locations, and can start with little warning, prompting evacuations.
journey.reaction: A wedding business telling me about wildfires and earthquakes in its own destination guide, with a date on it. That's the opposite of hiding the catch.

journey.quote: Most Crete weddings fall into one of three settings.
journey.reaction: 'Most' is a big word about every wedding on the island. 'Crete weddings tend to fall into' says the same thing without me raising an eyebrow.

journey.section: Six venues from east to west
journey.quote: Each has a full entry in our guide to the best Crete wedding venues, alongside the others we recommend.
journey.reaction: 'Recommend' on what basis? This is where I start wondering whether these venues pay you.

journey.section: Six venues from east to west
journey.quote: Not published: capacity or an exclusive-use option at St. Nicolas Bay, and capacity or a legal ceremony option at Caramel.
journey.reaction: They tell me what they don't know instead of filling the gap with a guess. That makes me trust the rest of the list more.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: The Elounda Collection, which covers Elounda Peninsula, Porto Elounda and Elounda Mare, makes its civil, Orthodox and symbolic packages valid only when the couple stays at least three nights in one of its hotels.
journey.reaction: There's the catch, named and pinned to a venue. That's the line I'd want to know before falling for a resort.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Euphoria Resort at Kolymvari sells complete packages whose items are not interchangeable: a service not used brings no refund or alternative, and amendments or custom packages cost extra.
journey.reaction: The 'you pay for it whether you use it or not' clause, spelled out. No spin on it.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Its civil package rate does not include the Municipal fees, and its Orthodox rate does not include the Metropolis fee, so those are charged on top.
journey.reaction: Fees outside the package. Exactly the stuff that shows up on the final invoice and nowhere else.

journey.quote: Which year's terms apply to our date, and when were they last updated?
journey.reaction: The whole list of ten is going in my spreadsheet, and this one is the question nobody thinks to ask.

journey.section: What drives the cost of a Crete wedding
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms the inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fine the first time. By the third version of this line (venues, costs, closing) it starts to sound like a sales script rather than information.

journey.quote: From Agios Nikolaos, Minos Beach Art Hotel puts Chania Airport at a 180-minute drive.
journey.reaction: An actual number backing up 'distances on Crete are real'. Useful for telling the in-laws which airport to book.

journey.quote: Four weeks before. Copies of the documents go to the Elounda Collection by email for approval at least 4 weeks before the date.
journey.reaction: The headings read like a general Greek timeline, but the steps are one resort's rules. I only worked that out when I hit 'Other venues set their own steps' at the end. Say it's the Elounda Collection's example up front.

journey.section: Plan your Crete wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't tell me how the fee is worked out or whether the venues pay you as well.

unanswered_questions: Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues?
How are the venues you 'recommend' chosen, and does a venue pay to be included?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee calculated and what exactly does it cover?
Is the first consultation free, and what do I get from it?
Do other Crete venues and municipalities work to similar document lead times as the Elounda Collection, or can they be very different?
Is there a real Crete wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: Each has a full entry in our guide to the best Crete wedding venues, alongside the others we recommend.
turn_offs_found.why: 'The best' and 'we recommend' with no word on how the list is chosen. For someone already worried about commissions baked into supplier prices, an unexplained recommendation is the first thing I'd check against other sites.

turn_offs_found.quote: Most Crete weddings fall into one of three settings.
turn_offs_found.why: A claim about every wedding on the island, stated as fact. It's probably fair, but 'most' is the kind of word I test, and softening it costs nothing.
It's the one answer on the page that reads like a pitch. The rest of the article is honest about heat, wildfires and travel time, so leaving those out of the FAQ answer makes it feel one-sided.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the ten questions to ask every venue, to send to the resorts on our list
Both sets of parents: the getting-there section, so they book the right airport

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, start planning with Wedded Concierge.
cta_reaction.why: The page did the work: sourced weather data, dated travel advice, the venues' own catches quoted, gaps admitted. The CTAs come after evidence, not before. What holds me back is the same thing as every planner: do you take a cut from the venues you recommend, and how is your fee worked out? The fee-in-writing line helps, but it doesn't answer that.

top_3_changes: Label the planning timeline's document steps as the Elounda Collection's example up front (for example 'At the Elounda Collection, for instance:' before 'Four weeks before'), so it doesn't read as a Greece-wide legal timetable.

Make the FAQ 'Is Crete good for a destination wedding?' answer honest both ways: keep the 'yes', then add the trade-offs the page already covers (July and August highs above 30 degrees in the west, wildfire season June to September, a three-hour drive between the two ends of the island).

Soften 'Most Crete weddings fall into one of three settings' to 'tend to fall into', and cut the 'confirms in writing before you commit' line from three mentions to one or two. (How recommended venues are chosen, commission and fee model would also help, but those are deferred business details, so nice-to-have.)

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and costs first, looked for catches, superlatives, fee model and commissions
No invented brand facts; commission, venue selection, fee model and first-call details placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (image slots, fact tags, CTA markers) ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'how we know' lines

open_questions.question: 'alongside the others we recommend' raises the commission question for this persona. Is a neutral rewording (for example 'alongside the other venues in that guide') in scope this round, or does it wait for the deferred business details?

assumptions: Daniel arrived via a Google search for 'wedding in crete' with Crete on the shortlist while comparing three planners.
No prices on the page, including the costs section, is by design and not penalised.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not assessed.
